calibrated_on: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), Ruby 4.0.9, rbs 4.2.0, release-gate run 41594749455 (bench-corpus-v0.4.7 @ f7595e289); wall_s carried from release-gate run 40107250867
note: Advanced from corpus v0.4.6 to v0.4.7 after the v0.4.7 release (2026-11-03). Linux CI measurements of the v0.4.7 engine (a branch cut at the tag, f7595e289) over the frozen corpus v0.4.7, release-gate run 41594749455: allocations 72,615,864 (rep 2: 72,632,948), peak_rss_kb 758,196 (reps 783,112 and 758,196, the lower kept), diagnostics 1. The previous baseline (corpus v0.4.6, refreshed after #2618) read 63,444,766 allocations and peak_rss_kb 647,748; the v0.4.7 release candidate measured 63,897,311 and 698,980 on that corpus (release-gate run 41579256529, attempt 2). The move is mostly corpus growth, lib growing from 617 to 649 files with the v0.4.7 changes, measured by the released engine; Ruby 4.0.9 and rbs 4.2.0 are unchanged from the previous calibration. wall_s is not the artifact's: the run measured 53.559 and 49.769 on a fast runner draw, and following the v0.4.6 ruling that wall_s is a coarse backstop never re-anchored on one draw, it keeps 56.472 (a 68 s ceiling) while allocations, peak_rss_kb and diagnostics come from this run. Previous calibration note: Refreshed on the same corpus v0.4.6 after the engine improvement #2618, measured at that PR's own merge commit f558448b0 (branch bench-refresh-2618, release-gate run 41481534538) as the "Refreshing after an improvement" section of bench/README.md requires. allocations 63,444,766 (rep 2: 63,448,852) replaces 65,033,529 (-2.44%); the run printed STALE (2.4% below the baseline). wall_s, peak_rss_kb and diagnostics are NOT taken from this run. wall_s keeps 56.472 per the v0.4.6 ruling: the run measured 81.779 and 81.204 on a slow runner draw and failed only the wall band, which bench/README.md treats as runner noise, never a reason to recalibrate. peak_rss_kb keeps 647,748: the run measured 684,168 (+5.6%, inside the +10% band), and re-anchoring it here would loosen the RSS ceiling as a side effect of an allocation refresh. diagnostics stays 1, which the run also measured. Per-PR "Engine allocations" warnings since the 2026-10-24 calibration (103 merged PRs, #2331 to #2618): no PR crossed pr_allocations_pct (1%). 42 PRs carried the cumulative "merged onto master" notice that projects the release gate (+2% band): #2373 to #2415 peaked at +2.91% (#2406) and fell back to +1.68% by #2420; #2516, #2554 and #2556 read +2.23% to +2.25% and fell back with #2557; the rest read +1.55% to +1.78%, the last +1.78% at #2616. #2618 answers the remainder by recovering 2.95M allocations (-4.06% on its A/B), so no warning stands unanswered. Engine changes merged after f558448b0 (#2623, +0.13% on its A/B) are not absorbed by this refresh and count against the new band. Previous calibration note (release-gate run 40107250867, 2026-10-24): Linux CI measurements of the v0.4.6 engine (a branch cut at the tag, 25e637732) over the frozen corpus v0.4.6: the tree at that tag, unpacked with git archive (#1507). allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. bench/README.md lists what the corpus run does not reproduce: gems' own sig/, the core RBS and Ruby, which come from the run, and a user-global BUNDLE_PATH. Advanced from corpus v0.4.5 after the v0.4.6 release (2026-10-23). The previous baseline (release-gate run 39886264420, the v0.4.6 release candidate on corpus v0.4.5) read 62,078,564 allocations, peak_rss_kb 632,152 and diagnostics 3, with wall_s held at 56.472 by the maintainer's v0.4.6 ruling. This run (40107250867) reads 65,033,529 allocations (+4.76%), peak_rss_kb 647,748 and diagnostics 1. The engine is the released one, so the move is corpus growth, lib growing from 598 to 617 files with the v0.4.6 changes, plus the Ruby patch the run installed (4.0.9, where the previous calibration ran 4.0.8); diagnostics falls to 1 because the v0.4.6 tree carries the tightened Scope optimistic_locals / optimistic_ivars declarations. wall_s is not the artifact's: the run measured 79.189 (reps 80.321 and 79.189) on a slow runner draw, and the v0.4.6 cut measured 41.6 to 77.0 s on one engine, so following the v0.4.6 ruling on the same point wall_s keeps 56.472 (a 68 s ceiling) while allocations, peak_rss_kb and diagnostics come from this run. The band is a budget for the engine cost added since this calibration. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement by measuring the improving PR's own merge commit, and list in the new note every per-PR warning since this calibration with its answer; an unanswered one needs the user's ruling first. A red cut clears only by attributing the rise and recalibrating on the same corpus on the user's ruling. After each release the corpus advances to the new tag. bench/README.md and the rigor-release-prep skill carry the procedures. Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
